name: UB City
subcategory: Mixed-use high-rise complex / luxury shopping mall
description: UB City is a mixed-use high-rise complex on a 13-acre site at the corner of Kasturba Road and Vittal Mallya Road in the central business district, directly opposite Cubbon Park and 1.8 km from the MG Road-Brigade Road junction. It comprises six buildings with over 1.6 million sq ft of built-up area, combining the luxury retail mall 'The Collection', corporate offices (including United Breweries' own UB Tower) and service apartments. Its four towers are named Concorde (the UB Tower, 20 floors, 123 m to roof), Canberra, Comet and a fourth slab, giving the complex a stepped, clustered skyline.
history: The development was established by the UB Group in a joint venture with the Prestige Group, with Prestige as main contractor, and construction began in 2004 with completion in 2008. The Times of India reported the project as 'finally here' in June 2006 while it was still being fitted out, and in June 2009 the Financial Express reported UB City winning an Asia-Pacific property award as a joint development venture between the two groups. The complex opened as India's first luxury shopping destination under the 'The Collection' banner, and UB Tower later gained an elevated rooftop helipad advertised as giving a five-minute aerial commute to Kempegowda International Airport.
facts: Six buildings on 13 acres, with a total built-up area of over 1.6 million sq ft (Wikipedia infobox lists 950,000 sq ft / 88,000 m2 of floor area).
The tallest tower, UB Tower / Concorde, has 20 floors and a roof height of 123 m (404 ft).
Roughly 1,000,000 sq ft (93,000 m2) of high-end commercial, retail and service-apartment space is hosted on the site.
UB Tower carries an elevated rooftop helipad offering a five-minute aerial commute to Kempegowda International Airport.

OpenStreetMap records the mall land-use polygon at 24 Vittal Mallya Road, 560001, with four tower blocks: Concorde (20 levels), Canberra (18 levels), Comet (11 levels) and an unnamed 19-level block of 50 m.
The site is bounded by Vittal Mallya Road to the east, Kasturba Road to the west and Cubbon Park opposite; the Bowring Institute stands just south along Vittal Mallya Road.

name: World Trade Center Bengaluru
description: The World Trade Center Bengaluru (WTCB) is a 32-storey, 128 m commercial tower in Malleshwaram West, near the ISKCON temple, Indian Institute of Science and Yeshvantpur Junction. Built by the Brigade Group under a World Trade Centers Association licence, it was the second World Trade Center in India after Mumbai and remains the tallest commercial building in Bengaluru. The tower sits inside the integrated Brigade Gateway enclave alongside Orion Mall, Manipal Hospital, the Sheraton hotel, a school and apartment blocks, with a skywalk bridge linking it to the Sheraton Grand Bangalore Hotel.
history: The tower was opened for operation in 2010, reported by The Hindu in August 2010, having been built by Brigade Group after obtaining the World Trade Centers Association construction licence. At 128 m it was the tallest commercial building in South India from 2010 until 2015 and the tallest building in the city between 2010 and 2013. The surrounding Brigade Gateway development, which also contains Orion Mall, Manipal Hospital, the Sheraton hotel and the Brigade Gateway Apartments, received recognition in The Hindu's property review in January 2011.

A skywalk bridge connects the tower to the Sheraton Grand Bangalore Hotel.

name: Bangalore International Exhibition Centre
description: BIEC is a large exhibition and convention complex on the 10th Mile of Tumkur Road, developed and managed by the Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers' Association (IMTMA). Wikipedia describes it as India's first LEED-certified green facility for exhibitions, conferences and B2B events, and it hosts everything from IMTEX and IIJS jewellery fairs to the Bengaluru Tech Summit and Excon. The official site lists a 77,200 sq m large exhibition facility with columnless halls spanning up to 75 metres and a 5,600 sq m large conference facility, with parking for 10,000 vehicles.
history: The centre was built and opened in 2007 as the permanent exhibition venue of IMTMA, replacing the association's earlier annual fairground model. It is sited beside the NICE corridor and the Bangalore-Nelamangala Expressway in north Bengaluru, with the Madavara metro station and bus stop on its doorstep on Namma Metro Reach 3. Since opening it has hosted more than 400 events, including many national and international exhibitions.

name: Manyata Tech Park
description: Manyata Tech Park is a roughly 300-acre IT and business park on the Outer Ring Road at Nagawara, close to Hebbal, developed by the Embassy Group under Embassy Office Parks. It holds about 9.8 million sq ft of building space and more than 150,000 professionals (as of November 2017), with major tenant campuses including IBM, Target, Nvidia, Rolls-Royce, Fidelity Investments, Philips and Continental. The park is laid out as a business district with corporate campuses, an employee garden, an 85-acre residential enclave (Manyata Residency) behind it and, in OpenStreetMap, 30-41 storey towers under construction alongside 34-storey residential slabs.
history: Manyata Tech Park was founded in 2001 and is operated by Embassy Office Parks, the listed real-estate arm of the Embassy Group. It quickly became one of Bengaluru's largest employer clusters and won the NDTV Property Awards' Best IT Park Award in 2013. Development has continued with the adjacent Karle SEZ and Karle Zenith residences, and OpenStreetMap currently records towers G, H, J, K, L and M under construction within the park.

name: Electronic City Phase 1
description: Electronic City Phase 1 is the first and original phase of the KEONICS industrial township on the western side of Hosur Road in south Bengaluru, and today forms the 'Electronic City West' half of the estate. It is the campus district for the IT majors - OpenStreetMap tags the Infosys blocks by number (B25/26, B30/31, B32/33, B34/35/36/37, B38/39/40/41), alongside BHEL, Hewlett Packard GlobalSoft, NTTF, Fanuc and a Terminal Food Court. The township as a whole houses around 200 IT and ITES company campuses, with main campuses of Infosys, Wipro, TCS, HCL, Tech Mahindra and Biocon, and is served by the Yellow Line metro.
history: Electronic City was the brainchild of R. K. Baliga (1929-1988), the first Chairman and Managing Director of KEONICS, Karnataka's electronics development corporation, who wanted to make Bengaluru the 'Silicon Valley of India'. KEONICS established the township in 1978 on 332 acres of land in the Konappana Agrahara and Doddathogur villages of Begur Hobli. Maintenance and upkeep passed to ELCITA, the Electronic City Township Industries Association, in 1997, and a notification of 18 March 2013 brought Phases I, II and III under the E-City Industrial Township Area. The estate grew to 903 acres and 11 guntas, with a further 122 acres acquired in 2003 to form Phase III, while Phase II covers about 340 acres.
facts: Phase 1 lies entirely on the western side of Hosur Road and forms 'Electronic City West'; the official township site places the estate at 12.85 N, 77.67 E on the Hosur Road (NH 7) corridor, about 9 km from Silk Board and 18 km from Vidhana Soudha.
Founded in 1978 on 332 acres in Konappana Agrahara and Doddathogur villages; the estate now covers 903 acres and 11 guntas over three phases.
Phase II covers about 340 acres and lies on both sides of Hosur Road; a further 122 acres acquired in 2003 formed Phase III.

Around 200 IT and ITES company campuses operate in Electronic City, including main campuses of Infosys, Wipro, TCS, HCL, Tech Mahindra and Biocon; major employers listed by Wikipedia include BHEL, Hewlett-Packard, Siemens, Continental, Genpact and Bosch.
A 9.985 km four-lane elevated expressway from Silk Board junction to Electronic City opened on 22 January 2010.

The 19.15 km elevated Yellow Line of Namma Metro (R.V. Road to Bommasandra, 16 stations) was inaugurated on 10 August 2025, with an Electronic City metro station, plus Konappana Agrahara station funded by the Infosys Foundation.
ELCITA, the township industries association, took over upkeep in 1997 and has deployed about 500 security officials with CCTV on strategic locations.

OpenStreetMap maps the Phase 1 Infosys campus in numbered blocks - B25/26, B30/31, B32/33, B34/35/36/37 and B38/39/40/41 - together with an Infosys fountain park, an Infosys skywalk, Hewlett Packard Avenue, the BHEL campus, NTTF and a Terminal Food Court.

name: Kempegowda International Airport
description: Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) is the airport serving Bengaluru, located at Devanahalli about 35 km north of the city centre at an elevation of 915 m. It has two passenger terminals: a domestic-only Terminal 1 and the much larger Terminal 2, which was designed as a tribute to the city's 'Garden City' identity by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill and built by Larsen & Toubro. Two parallel 4,000 m x 45 m asphalt runways (09L/27R and 09R/27L) carry CAT IIIB instrument approaches, and the airport is described as Karnataka's first fully solar-powered airport.
history: The airport opened on 24 May 2008, its first commercial arrival being Air India flight AI609 from Mumbai on 23 May, having been developed at an initial estimated cost of about 1,930 crore rupees. It was originally named Bengaluru International Airport; Karnataka proposed the Kempe Gowda name in February 2009, the Union accepted it in 2012, formal approval came in July 2013 and the official renaming took effect on 14 December 2013, when the expanded terminal was inaugurated. Terminal 2, designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill and constructed by Larsen & Toubro at a cost of about 5,000 crore rupees, was inaugurated on 11 November 2022, began operations in January 2023 and took over all international flights on 12 September 2023.
facts: Opened 24 May 2008; first commercial arrival was Air India flight AI609 from Mumbai on 23 May 2008. Renamed Kempegowda International Airport on 14 December 2013, honouring the city's founder Kempe Gowda I.
Site elevation of 915 m, about 35 km north of central Bengaluru.
Terminal 1 has been domestic-only since September 2023, with a listed capacity of 35 million passengers a year, and was enlarged to 150,556 sq m.
Terminal 2 Phase 1 covers 255,000 sq m and adds 25 million passengers of annual capacity; a second phase is planned to add another 20 million.
Stated combined capacity of 55-60 million passengers a year after Terminal 2.
Two parallel asphalt runways, 09L/27R and 09R/27L, each 4,000 m long and 45 m wide, both with CAT IIIB instrument landing systems; the northern runway achieved full CAT IIIB capability in May 2025.
Costs: initial airport build about 1,930 crore rupees; first terminal expansion about 1,500 crore; broader second expansion about 4,000 crore; Terminal 2 Phase 1 about 5,000 crore rupees.
Karnataka's first fully solar-powered airport; the cargo village has space for nearly 80 trucks.
OpenStreetMap records Terminal 1 as a transportation building of roughly 714 m x 210 m and an air traffic control tower 65 m tall.

name: Indian Institute of Management Bangalore
description: IIM Bangalore is the third Indian Institute of Management, established in 1973 and now an Institute of National Importance under the IIM Act 2017, with its 105-acre Bannerghatta Road campus in Bilekahalli. The campus was designed by B. V. Doshi as a 'poly-nuclear' plan of low blocks, passageways, pergolas and open quadrangles inspired by Fatehpur Sikri and the Meenakshi Temple, and its planting - 62 acres of green cover, about 30,000 trees and more than 50 groundwater recharge wells - was the founding director's way of expressing Bengaluru as 'green and alive'. The library occupies four levels and 55,000 sq ft, and the campus also hosts the 18,000 sq ft NSRCEL entrepreneurship centre.
history: Design work began in 1977 with B. V. Doshi through his practice Stein, Doshi & Bhalla, assisted by Kanvinde & Rai, and original construction concluded in 1983. The poly-nuclear design combined Indian traditional planning with Team 10 modernist principles and was later placed among T magazine's 25 significant postwar works. The institute has since added a new classroom complex of about 6,500 sq m designed by Sanjay Mohe's Mindspace Architects, a 110-acre second campus near Jigani in Anekal Taluka about 20 km from the main campus, and a Management Development Centre at Jigani that opened on 1 March 2023; an IIMB station on the Namma Metro Pink Line was planned for March 2026.
facts: Established in 1973; the third IIM in the country, and an Institute of National Importance under the IIM Act 2017.
Main campus of about 105 acres (42 hectares) on Bannerghatta Road, with a second 110-acre campus near Jigani in Anekal Taluka about 20 km away.
Original academic complex of about 54,000 sq m; green cover of 62 acres with roughly 30,000 trees and more than 50 groundwater-recharge wells.

Central library of four levels and 55,000 sq ft, holding more than 163,000 printed books, 9,000 journals, over 42,000 periodical issues and access to more than 110 electronic databases; renovated 2016-19.
New Classroom Complex of about 6,500 sq m designed by Sanjay Mohe of Mindspace Architects; the NSRCEL building is 18,000 sq ft.
109 academic staff; the 2016 IIM Management Review is published quarterly through Elsevier; the IIMBx Open edX platform was launched in 2014.
Accredited by EFMD EQUIS since 2010; ranked second among Indian management institutes by NIRF in 2024 and 57th globally by the Financial Times for its MBA in 2025.
The campus also includes an academic block, a central pergola, an amphitheatre, a computer centre, hostel block L-Square and the library.

name: Christ University
description: Christ University is a private deemed university in Bengaluru founded in 1969 as Christ College by the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate (CMI) congregation, granted UGC autonomy in 2004 and declared a deemed university in 2008. The flagship and main campus selected for this entry is the Bangalore Central Campus on Hosur Road, standing on 25 acres within the larger 100-acre Dharmaram Campus; the Bannerghatta Road campus at Hulimavu (opened May 2016) is a second, separate campus. The university runs a wide portfolio of UG, PG and doctoral programmes with 30,777 students, including about 700 international students from 58 nationalities.
history: The institution traces its educational vision to St. Kuriakose Elias Chavara, who founded the CMI congregation in 1831, and was founded by the congregation in 1969 as Christ College on the Dharmaram campus. It received UGC autonomy in 2004 and deemed-university status in 2008; the chancellor is Rev. Dr. Saju Chackalackal. The Bannerghatta Road campus at Hulimavu was inaugurated in May 2016, and the university has since expanded to Kengeri (90 acres), Yeshwanthpur (1.6 million sq ft), Pune Lavasa (28 acres) and a Delhi NCR-Ghaziabad site (5 acres).

13 km from Majestic/KSR City/Cantt railway stations and 44 km from Kempegowda International Airport; an IIMB station on the Pink Line was planned for March 2026.

name: Magrath Road
description: Magrath Road is a short commercial street in central Bengaluru, in the Sampangi Rama Nagar and Ashok Nagar block immediately behind Mayo Hall, and is part of the nineteenth-century Cantonment street grid. It is named after Colonel John Richard Magrath of the Royal Madras Artillery, and historically served as 'the stomping ground of the British military elite'; today it is a busy retail and services street known for the traffic jams at the Garuda Mall approach. OpenStreetMap records roughly 930 metres of named carriageway here, with the Mallya Hospital and the District Court complex close by.
history: The street formed part of the ordered Cantonment grid laid out when the British military and its families settled in Bangalore after 1809, and it was named for Colonel John Richard Magrath of the Royal Madras Artillery, who later became an Assistant to the Director-General of Telegraphs; after retiring from Bangalore to Ireland he reputedly owned the only car then in Ireland, a 3.5 hp Benz Dogcart registered MI 1. Its western end is anchored by Mayo Hall, the two-storey memorial to Viceroy Richard Bourke, built in 1878-79 and inaugurated by the British Resident on 6 June 1883 at a cost of about 45,000 rupees raised largely through public donations. In more recent times the street has been the subject of a municipal facelift: The Times of India reported a 'new look' with wider footpaths and better drains across a 350-metre stretch.
facts: OpenStreetMap records about 930 metres of named carriageway for Magrath Road within the central block: a 488 m primary segment plus secondary and tertiary segments of 65 m, 55 m, 64 m and 12 m.
Named after Colonel John Richard Magrath of the Royal Madras Artillery, who later served as an Assistant to the Director-General of Telegraphs.
Magrath reputedly owned the only car in Ireland after retiring to that country - a 3.5 hp Benz Dogcart with registration MI 1.
The street was part of the Cantonment grid and was historically the 'stomping ground of the British military elite'; more recently it has been described as the gateway to Garuda Mall's traffic jams.

Mayo Hall, the two-storey memorial to Viceroy Richard Bourke, was inaugurated on 6 June 1883, cost about 45,000 rupees largely raised by public subscription, and stands at the western end of the street; the Bangalore District Gazetteer praised its 'architrave and pedimented windows, varied with key-storied arches' and 'typical Greek cornice'.
Mayo Hall now houses the municipal offices of the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and the Kempegowda Museum, established in 2011 on the upper floor.
The Times of India reported a 2025 facelift of the street with wider footpaths and improved drains across a 350-metre stretch.

name: Bannerghatta Road (Karnataka State Highway 87)
description: Bannerghatta Road is Karnataka State Highway 87, the main arterial running south from the Hosur Road junction at Adugodi through Bilekahalli, Arekere, Hulimavu and Gottigere to Jigani and Anekal at the Tamil Nadu border. It is the spine of south Bengaluru, carrying the IIM Bangalore campus and Christ University's Hulimavu campus, the Jayadeva, Apollo, Fortis and Narayana hospitals, and the Vega City, Royal Meenakshi, Shoppers Stop and Gopalan mall cluster, with the Namma Metro Pink Line running along it to IIMB. The corridor carries the elevated NICE expressway interchange near Gottigere and the Bangalore-Mysore Infrastructure Corridor crossing.
history: The highway was originally laid as the road from Bangalore to Bannerghatta, then extended through Jigani to Anekal and on to Samanduru at the Tamil Nadu state boundary, where it continues as a Major District Road and merges with National Highway 948 A. In 2011 the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike announced selective widening of the road from 20-25 metres to 45 metres together with underpasses and flyovers at major junctions, at an estimated cost of 137 crore rupees. Grade separation followed with the Dairy Circle and Jayadeva underpasses, and for about five kilometres south of the Jayadeva Underpass the road was widened to four lanes by Mantri Developers in one of Bengaluru's earliest public-private partnership infrastructure projects. The Pink Line of the Namma Metro was then routed along the corridor, from Kalena Agrahara to Nagawara via IIMB, to take traffic off the road.
facts: Designated Karnataka State Highway 87, also called the Jigani-Anekal Road and the Anekal-Hosur Road; it links Bengaluru with Bannerghatta, Jigani and Anekal.
Length given as 45 km in the article text and 49 km in the infobox.

Northern terminus at Adugodi, where it branches from Hosur Road near the Adugodi Christian Cemetery; southern terminus at Samanduru in Anekal taluk at the Tamil Nadu border, continuing in Tamil Nadu as an MDR merging with NH 948 A.
2011 upgrade plan: widening from 20-25 m to 45 m with underpasses and flyovers, at an estimated cost of 137 crore rupees.
Two grade-separated underpasses exist on the corridor: the Dairy Circle Underpass and the Jayadeva Underpass; a flyover sits at Dairy Circle.
About five kilometres south of the Jayadeva Underpass the road was widened to four lanes by Mantri Developers under one of Bengaluru's earliest public-private partnerships.
Major intersections: Hosur Road at Adugodi, Marigowda Road at Dairy Circle, Marenahalli Road and the Outer Ring Road at the Jayadeva Hospital interchange, and the NICE corridor near Gottigere.
The Outer Ring Road runs concurrently with Bannerghatta Road from the Jayadeva Hospital Interchange to JD Mara Junction in front of Vega City Mall before diverging towards Electronic City.

Institutions on the corridor include IIM Bangalore (between Bilekahalli and Arekere) and Christ University's Dairy Circle and Hulimavu campuses; hospitals include Sri Jayadeva Institute, Apollo, Fortis and Narayana Health; malls include Gopalan Innovation Mall, Shoppers Stop, Vega City and Royal Meenakshi Mall.
The Namma Metro Pink Line runs from Kalena Agrahara to Nagawara along the corridor via IIMB.
Note for modellers: the current National Highway 12 runs entirely within West Bengal and does not include this corridor - Bannerghatta Road is a state highway, not an NH 12 route.
